purpose: Mint speaker B once, freeze it, and prove it is one voice and a different person from A before 240 turns depend on it.

decision.caption: 落ち着いた成人男性の声。標準的な話し方で、感情を抑えて自然に読み上げてください。
decision.used_as: --ref-wav for every speaker-B turn in both V-real and V-tts

watermark.mechanism: experiments/tsukuyomi_ojousama/m3/nowatermark/ first on PYTHONPATH; import silentcipher raises ImportError, which irodori_tts/watermark.py handles
watermark.verified: 'silentcipher_watermark' appears 0 times and 'not be watermarked' 3 times in ref/mint.log, and 0/12 in ref-consistency/gen.log
watermark.why: The watermark is an injected signal that would sit in every synthetic turn of both datasets while V-real's channel A carries none - a systematic difference on top of the one the comparison isolates.

calibration_band.note: A within-group similarity means nothing without knowing what one real human scores under the same pipeline.

gates.result: All three candidates passed every gate. Selection went to the highest consistency, which also had the best separation.

measurement_note: Consistency was measured under --ref-wav, the condition the dataset actually uses, and the reference clip itself is included in the group because every later turn is conditioned on it. The earlier probe measured --no-ref per utterance and scored 0.4525-0.5176, below the human floor.
limits: Five clips per candidate is a small group. The full 240-turn render is gated again at plan step 11 over the pooled B turns, where n is large enough for a percentile.
